title: GadgetlyHome
summary: A smart home planner that starts from your home and its annoyances, not from products

thumbnail.alt: Play a day: a floor plan and a timeline showing what each device does through the day

role: Research, UX, UI, prototyping and build
problem: Smart home shopping starts with products, not with your home. I asked r/smarthome how people decide what to buy. The post got 13K views and 30 comments, and the strongest pattern in the 19 real answers was to start from an annoyance, not a device. People also distrusted tools that claim to know better.
approach: So I designed GadgetlyHome around that. You tap the rooms that bother you, and devices appear where they help, each with a plain reason you can keep or remove. Then you “play a day” to see what each one does, and leave with a priced, ordered plan and where to buy. Solar is sized down to the panel. No account needed.
highlights: Four flow framings built and compared
A planned A/B test to raise sign-up confirmation

title: Caria
summary: Car rental comparison platform unifying offers, booking processes, and fleet management for Tunisian agencies.

thumbnail.alt: Caria vehicle page with prices and rental dates, over the agency reservations dashboard

overview: Caria resolves agency fragmentation by offering a unified booking and search platform. Renters can locate, compare, and reserve vehicles through a simplified, reliable UI.
problem: Renting a car in Tunisia required comparing offers across multiple agencies, creating a fragmented user experience.

sections.title: Research & Discovery
body: Conducted interviews with renters and local car rental owners to map out pricing schemas, availability constraints, and typical trust barriers.

sections.title: UX Strategy
body: Designed a car rental comparison platform allowing users to compare vehicles, prices, and agencies from a single interface.

sections.title: Design System
body: Developed a modern layout engine with custom filter panels, detailed comparison tables, and agency review badges.

outcome: Created a unified comparison experience that simplified the car rental search and booking process.

title: Transit Management Platform
summary: Real-time dispatch, route monitoring, and operational compliance platform customized for ZATCA’s requirements.

thumbnail.alt: Transit Management System: the driver app on a phone beside the live fleet map

overview: The Transit Management Platform empowers operators to monitor vehicles, trips, and overall transit operations in real time. The project successfully tailored the interface to ZATCA’s operational regulations while drastically improving dispatcher ergonomics.
problem: Operators struggled to monitor vehicles, trips, and transit operations in real time, making daily operations difficult to manage efficiently and causing compliance delays.

sections.title: Research & Discovery
body: Conducted contextual inquiries with dispatch managers and shadowed operations teams to understand high-stress telemetry monitoring, cognitive load, and routing priorities.

sections.title: UX Strategy
body: Designed a real-time transit management platform with interactive maps, zone management, trip monitoring, operational dashboards, and a companion mobile app for drivers.

sections.title: Design System
body: Developed a telemetry-oriented UI kit with unified status indicators, clear typography scale for mapping interfaces, and highly visible interactive alert nodes.

outcome: Improved the user experience and successfully customized the platform to meet ZATCA’s operational requirements.

title: LRT Cloud
summary: Centralized SaaS dashboard for charging station telemetry, automated reimbursements, and energy grid load balancing.

thumbnail.alt: LRT Cloud energy systems view in front of the reports screen

overview: LRT Cloud is a centralized platform for managing charging stations, users, organizations, subscriptions, reimbursements, and energy systems, helping operators track load distribution and billing.
problem: EV charging operators lacked a centralized way to monitor charging stations, users, and energy consumption in a unified interface.

sections.title: Research & Discovery
body: Audited energy management standards and surveyed station operators to map the core billing and maintenance workflow loops.

sections.title: UX Strategy
body: Designed a cloud platform for managing charging stations, users, organizations, subscriptions, reimbursements, and energy systems.

sections.title: Design System
body: Created a component framework with telemetry sparklines, consumption badges, and subscription/pricing builder patterns.

outcome: Accelerated product readiness by designing scalable workflows for charging management, reimbursements, subscriptions, and energy systems.

title: PowerUp Mobile App
summary: Reimagined EV charging app focusing on seamless hardware onboarding, instant map payments, and charging logs.

thumbnail.alt: PowerUp app on three phones: an active charging session, a session summary and a charging station on the map

overview: The PowerUp mobile app delivers an intuitive onboarding and charger setup experience. The redesign addresses major onboarding bottlenecks and provides streamlined public charging paths.
problem: Users found public charging and charger setup unnecessarily complex, leading to friction during onboarding and charging sessions.

sections.title: Research & Discovery
body: Conducted card sorting, interactive remote usability tests, and user interviews to isolate key points of drop-off during the initial Bluetooth charger pairing sequence.

sections.title: UX Strategy
body: Redesigned the mobile experience focusing on charger setup, public charging, user engagement, and growth-focused UX improvements.

sections.title: Design System
body: Constructed a high-contrast mobile design system optimized for outdoor visibility, featuring friendly helper illustrations and large touch targets.

outcome: Improved the charging experience through a redesigned onboarding flow and growth-focused user journeys.

title: PTS Redesign
summary: An internal project management tool, simplified through research and streamlined workflows.

thumbnail.alt: PTS project overview with sprint charts, surrounded by a task card, a create menu and a status legend

overview: The PTS Redesign focused on simplifying internal project management systems. By analyzing team behaviors and streamlining workflows, we transformed a complex application into an operational tool.
problem: Users struggled with a complex interface and inefficient workflows that slowed daily operations.

sections.title: Research & Discovery
body: Performed shadowing, workflow diagram audits, and user surveys to identify where multi-team handoffs failed or became blocked.

sections.title: UX Strategy
body: Redesigned the platform using user research, improved information architecture, and simplified workflows for internal project management.

sections.title: Design System
body: Rebuilt the dashboard theme with modular task tables, notification center models, and clean dashboard stats.

outcome: Research insights helped streamline task management and improve collaboration between multiple teams.
